candidate: desktop-stream-fixes with incremental single-table worker projector
environment: Windows x64, HeadlessChrome 153.0.0.0, document.visibilityState=visible, Vite production build, same browser process
method: Fresh document context, 1000 and 2000 rows; baseline then worker for each size; initial render excluded, five appended rows measured. Same Markdown inputs in each baseline/worker pair. Samples rounded to 0.1 ms. Baseline excludes its old boundary-worker overhead.

metrics.formatReadyMs: Expected table row count committed, then next animation frame; excludes explicit 20ms observation delay
metrics.maxTimerDelayMs: Largest excess delay of a 10ms heartbeat in each sample
metrics.renderMs: Omitted: React Profiler is disabled in production

interpretation: Same-run formatting-ready median improved by 90.1% for 54KB and 96.0% for 109KB; maximum samples fell from 161.5 to 26.8ms and 631.2 to 43.6ms respectively.
Compare baseline and worker within this run. Absolute baseline timing differs from the earlier trial, so cross-run ratios are not used.
The earlier full-reparse worker regression is preserved in streaming-rendering-benchmark.json, not overwritten.

Benefit is for append-only single GFM tables. Document replacement, extra top-level blocks and Future-reference contexts use the complete parser. Initial table parsing is not accelerated by the row checkpoint.
This is a five-update synthetic browser experiment, not native Tauri latency, a production percentile, a memory benchmark or proof of acceleration for every Markdown construct.
